title: Graph
body:

The most general structure in [[INFORMATION STRUCTURES]]: a set of [[Vertices]] and a set of
edges joining pairs of them, with no other rules. Anything can connect to anything, cycles
are allowed, and there is no root. A [[Tree]] is the special case with no cycles and one
path between any two nodes; a [[Linked List]] is the special case where every vertex has at
most one neighbour forward.

That generality is the point. Road networks, social networks, web pages and their links,
task dependencies, state machines, and the call graph of a program are all graphs, and none
of them fit a hierarchy.

$$G = (V, E)$$

## Vocabulary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Degree | edges touching a vertex; in-degree and out-degree if [[Directed Graph\|directed]] |
| Path | a sequence of vertices joined by edges |
| Cycle | a path returning to its start |
| Connected | some path exists between every pair of vertices |
| Dense | $E$ close to $V^2$ |
| Sparse | $E$ close to $V$, which is most real graphs |
| Acyclic | no cycles; a directed acyclic graph (DAG) is the shape of a dependency list |

## Representation

Two choices, and the pick is a space-versus-time trade rather than a matter of taste:

| | [[Adjacency Matrix]] | [[Adjacency List]] |
|---|---|---|
| Space | $O(V^2)$ | $O(V + E)$ |
| Edge test $u \to v$ | $O(1)$ | $O(\deg u)$ |
| List neighbours of $u$ | $O(V)$ | $O(\deg u)$ |
| Best for | dense graphs, constant edge queries | sparse graphs, traversal |

## Traversal

The two workhorse traversals are breadth-first search, which fans out level by level using a
[[Queue]], and depth-first search, which follows one path as far as it goes using a
[[Stack]] (or [[Recursion]], which is the same stack). Both are $O(V + E)$ on an adjacency
list. Both need a visited set: unlike a [[Tree]], a graph has cycles, and a traversal
without one loops forever.

Neither has its own note in this vault yet, and nor do shortest paths or Dijkstra's
algorithm. They belong to [[ALGORITHMS AND COMPLEXITY]].

## Where it gets hard

Graph problems split sharply. Connectivity, traversal, shortest path, and
[[Minimum Spanning Tree]] are all polynomial and comfortable. [[Hamiltonian Cycle]],
graph colouring, and travelling salesman are [[NP-Complete]], and the graphs are not
noticeably different. That cliff is the subject of [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTABILITY]].
